title: Blondel Searches for King Richard
text:
In December 1192, returning from the Third Crusade, King Richard I of England was shipwrecked and tried to cross central Europe in disguise. Near Vienna he was recognized and seized by Duke Leopold of Austria, whom he had insulted at Acre. Richard was handed over to the Holy Roman Emperor Henry VI, who held him for a huge ransom. These facts are history.

A legend first written down in the 13th century, in the collection known as the Tales of a Minstrel of Reims, adds a story. Richard's minstrel Blondel, it says, did not know where his master was held, and set out to find him. He wandered from castle to castle across Germany and Austria. At each one he sang beneath the walls a song that he and Richard had composed together.

At last, at one castle, he sang the first verse and heard a voice from a high window answer with the second. It was the king. Blondel hurried home with the news, and Richard was soon ransomed.

In reality, Richard's whereabouts were soon widely known, and he was released in 1194 after England paid an enormous ransom.
lesson: Loyalty that keeps searching for a lost friend, even without a map, is a kind of love worth remembering. Do not give up on people who have vanished from view.
people: Blondel de Nesle, Richard I of England
caveat: The Blondel episode is a legend; the capture and ransom of Richard are historical.
